query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Implement an on‐the‐fly machine-learning potential (MLP) that is dynamically trained on ab initio liquid configurations at high temperatures to serve as the reference potential in thermodynamic integration.
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent HEA (e.g., nearly equimolar Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni) in the highly-disordered liquid state near and above its melting temperature.
generation.intervention: Replace the fixed EAM reference with an MLP that is periodically retrained using a selected ensemble of ab initio configurations sampled from high-temperature liquid MD trajectories.
generation.conditions: Applicable on the solid and liquid phases for HEA compositions around equiatomic ratios (e.g., with 5 or more components) and at temperatures from just below the melting point (~0.9 Tm) up to ~1.2 Tm.
generation.structural_mediator: The MLP implicitly captures the diverse many-body atomic interactions and the fluctuating local environments characteristic of the liquid state.
generation.mechanism: By learning from ab initio data that fully captures electronic-structure-driven interactions, the MLP will better represent the wide range of atomic configurations in the liquid, thereby improving the reference–target phase-space overlap. This is expected to reduce the mismatch along the thermodynamic integration (TI) path compared to TOR-TILD’s fixed EAM references because the MLP’s free-energy surface more closely tracks that of the ab initio liquid.
generation.predicted_outcome: A significant reduction (tentatively on the order of 30–50% based on analogous improvements seen in elemental liquids) in the TI path mismatch, leading to free-energy differences that more accurately approach ab initio predictions.
generation.baseline: TOR-TILD’s techniques using fixed EAM references calibrated on solid-state properties or limited liquid configurations.
generation.boundary: If the HEA composition has extremely large atomic size disparities or electronic effects that cannot be efficiently captured by current MLP descriptors, the intervention might underperform.
generation.uncertainty: The exact quantitative reduction in TI mismatch remains uncertain without pilot testing and may depend on the complexity of the liquid’s configuration space.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform parallel free-energy calculations for a high-temperature liquid HEA using (a) the traditional EAM reference via TOR-TILD and (b) the MLP-enhanced reference. The MLP should be trained on ab initio data from representative liquid configurations.
measurements: Free-energy differences computed via thermodynamic integration
Phase-space overlap metrics (e.g., distributions of potential energy and forces)

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the free-energy mismatch reduction does not exceed a statistically significant threshold (e.g., less than 20% improvement over TOR-TILD’s EAM reference), or if the phase-space overlap metrics are not improved, the hypothesis is falsified.

The MD simulations for investigating the structure of the Al0.1CrCoFeNi HEA have previously employed LJ potentials that cannot offer reliable predictions for such multi-component systems. Here, we assimilate the EAM/alloy potential parameters for Al, Co, Fe and Ni from the EAM database to model the elemental cross and self-interactions. Also, the cross interactions of Ni-Cr and Fe-Cr and the self-interactions of Cr-Cr are described with the EAM/alloy potential. Only the Al-Cr and Co-Cr cross interactions are modeled, using the Lennard-Jones (LJ) potential, due to the lack of the available EAM/alloy parameters for these interactions. In physics, the terms order and disorder designate the presence or absence of some symmetry or correlation in a many-particle system. In condensed matter physics, systems typically are ordered at low temperatures; upon heating, they undergo one or several phase transitions into less ordered states. Examples for such an order-disorder transition are: the melting of ice: solid-liquid transition, loss of crystalline order; the demagnetization of iron by heating above the Curie temperature: ferromagnetic-paramagnetic transition, loss of magnetic order. The degree of freedom that is ordered or disordered can be translational (crystalline ordering), rotational (ferroelectric ordering), or a spin state (magnetic ordering). The order can consist either in a full crystalline space group symmetry, or in a correlation. Depending on how the correlations decay with distance, one speaks of long range order or short range order. If a disordered state is not in thermodynamic equilibrium, one speaks of quenched disorder. top3.builds_on: The active learning and deep learning potential training approach demonstrated in the melting simulations of high-entropy carbonitrides (PMC11576752::web::007–PMC11576752::web::010).
top3.what_is_new: This hypothesis proposes directly substituting the EAM reference with an actively learned DNN potential to improve phase-space overlap for TI, rather than merely adjusting simulation parameters, offering a concrete methodological change with a clear benchmark based on free-energy integration paths.

fields.hypothesis: Replace the conventional EAM reference potential with a deep neural network (DNN) potential trained via active learning to more accurately capture the diverse atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid phase of high-entropy alloys.
fields.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high-entropy alloys (e.g., (TiZrTaHfNb)C1-xNx) near their high melting temperatures, both in solid and liquid states.
fields.intervention: Implement a DNN potential (using frameworks like DeepMD) trained with an active learning cycle that targets both solid and liquid configurations, replacing the traditional EAM reference in thermodynamic integration paths.
fields.conditions: Applicable for high-entropy alloys with compositions spanning refractory carbonitrides (x between 0 and 1) at temperatures from about 3000 K up to 5000 K.
fields.structural_mediator: The DNN potential is tuned to capture detailed short-range and many-body interactions that define the structural motifs (e.g., pair correlations, bond formation) in both phases.
fields.mechanism: Because the DNN potential is trained on ab initio data sampled through iterative active learning (as demonstrated in PMC11576752::web::007–PMC11576752::web::010), it can represent the vast configurational diversity of the liquid state. This improved representation enhances the phase-space overlap with the target ab initio potential, thereby reducing the mismatch along the thermodynamic integration (TI) pathway relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references.
fields.predicted_outcome: A significant reduction in the TI path mismatch is anticipated; estimates suggest a potential drop in free-energy integration errors by roughly 40–60% compared to standard EAM references, though the exact magnitude is uncertain.
fields.baseline: TOR-TILD’s EAM references, which are limited in representing the diverse atomic configurations in the liquid state.
fields.boundary: The method is expected to work for systems where ab initio sampling can feasibly cover high-temperature liquid configurations; extreme cases with very rapid atomic rearrangements or highly reactive species may require further model adaptations.
fields.uncertainty: Quantitative reduction in error is estimated from trends in high-entropy carbonitride studies, but exact percentage improvements will depend on the quality and extent of the active learning dataset.

top3.builds_on: The paper demonstrates that neural network frameworks can capture complex atomic diffusion barriers in ordered systems; this builds on that concept by using a GNN to tackle the greater diversity in liquid configurations.
top3.what_is_new: This hypothesis proposes the use of a graph neural network potential—with its inherent ability to handle disorder and many-body correlations—to improve the phase-space overlap in TI for high-entropy alloy liquids, an approach not addressed in the paper.

fields.hypothesis: Replace the plain EAM reference potential with a Graph Neural Network (GNN)–based interatomic potential that is trained specifically on a diverse set of ab initio liquid configurations featuring high entropy and structural disorder.
fields.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high-entropy alloys in the solid and liquid state at and above their high melting temperatures; presently modeled using standard EAM potentials that cannot capture the full diversity of high-temperature liquid configurations.
fields.intervention: Develop and implement a GNN potential that uses atomistic graph representations to encode many-body interactions and local disorder. The training dataset is enriched with ab initio molecular dynamics snapshots sampled from the liquid state over a range of temperatures near and above the melting point.
fields.conditions: Applicable for alloys with equimolar or near-equimolar compositions (e.g., NbMoTa-type systems) and temperature regimes spanning from just below the melting point (high-temperature solid) to fully molten liquid states.
fields.structural_mediator: The GNN descriptor effectively captures local atomic environments as graphs, representing variable coordination and bonding even in disordered states, thus serving as a continuous and adaptable mediator between structured and disordered phases.
fields.mechanism: Graph neural networks naturally incorporate permutation invariance and can learn nonlocal many-body correlations. By training on a wide variety of ab initio liquid configurations, the GNN potential will produce a smoother, more accurate representation of the liquid’s potential energy surface. This improved description enhances the phase-space overlap between the reference and target systems in thermodynamic integration, leading to a reduced integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references.
fields.predicted_outcome: A measurable reduction in the thermodynamic integration path mismatch; preliminary trends (from elemental and binary studies using machine-learned potentials) suggest potential improvements on the order of 30–40% relative to standard EAM, though precise values remain uncertain.
fields.baseline: TOR-TILD free-energy integration employing static EAM references.
fields.boundary: If the free-energy differences obtained via TI with the GNN potential do not converge closer to ab initio benchmarks than those with EAM—i.e., if the mismatch remains as high as with EAM—the hypothesis would be falsified.
fields.uncertainty: The exact percentage reduction in TI path mismatch is uncertain and will depend on the quality and breadth of the ab initio training dataset as well as the architecture of the GNN.

Compare the integration path smoothness and free-energy convergence against a fully ab initio TI benchmark.
measurements: Integrated free-energy differences as a function of TI path coordinate
Statistical variance in free energy along the path

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the GNN potential does not yield significantly lower integration path mismatch (i.e. free-energy differences outside the error bars of the ab initio benchmark remain comparable to those of EAM), the hypothesis is refuted.
